# PETROCOGNITORS

# FloodGuard AI

## IoT Driven Intelligent Flood Monitoring and Early Warning System

### IIT Bombay Hackathon Project Report

Team Name colon PetroCognitors. Project Name colon FloodGuard AI. Theme colon IoT driven intelligent flood monitoring and early warning. Study corridor colon Mithi River from BKC to Kurla in Mumbai Maharashtra India.

Team Lead colon Kavya Bumiya serving as AI slash ML Lead. Team Member Anish Chand Gupta serving as DevOps Engineer plus API Architect. Team Member Zankhana Rajput serving as Frontend Engineer. Team Member Palak Modha serving as IoT Engineer. Team Member Ahmad Abdullah serving as Backend Engineer.

This report documents an end to end platform that connects field sensing to cloud ingestion to intelligent analytics to live visualization to alerting. The report is written for hackathon judges who must understand the product in minutes and trust the engineering in depth. Every claim in this report is grounded in the as built codebase found in the backend directory the Frontend directory the config directory the models directory the data directory the infra directory and the docs directory.

How to read this report. Start with the Executive Summary for a one page understanding. Continue to Problem Statement and Our Solution for context. Continue to System Architecture IoT Backend AI Frontend Cloud Security Demonstration Testing Innovation Team Future Scope and Conclusion for depth. The report avoids tables and diagrams by deliberate instruction and instead explains every structure every flow and every interface in precise prose and enumerated lists so that the narrative remains accessible without visual aids.

Cover context note 1. FloodGuard AI was built for rapid flood onset where minutes matter. The team chose a corridor approach focused on Mithi River BKC to Kurla with representative coordinates near latitude 19 point 0713 and longitude 72 point 8830. The bounding study area spans approximately latitude 19 point 05 to 19 point 09 and longitude 72 point 85 to 72 point 90. The terrain raster used for simulation is a clipped DEM covering longitude 72 point 86 to 72 point 89 and latitude 19 point 06 to 19 point 085 with about 30 point 92 metre resolution. The report keeps this geographic grounding visible in every layer from ingestion to map to three dimensional twin.

# 1. Executive Summary

FloodGuard AI is an intelligent IoT based flood monitoring and early warning platform designed to provide real time environmental monitoring risk assessment and actionable alerts. The system combines IoT sensor nodes cloud hosted APIs backend data processing AI slash ML based flood risk analysis and a real time frontend dashboard. Sensor data is securely transmitted from field devices to a cloud hosted backend where it is validated stored analyzed and presented to users through an intuitive dashboard. The platform is designed to enable early detection of hazardous water level conditions and support faster decision making during flood events.

Executive summary elaboration 1. The problem is that floods develop rapidly while traditional monitoring can be delayed geographically limited and difficult to interpret. Raw centimetres and millimetres per hour do not tell an operator whether to watch to prepare or to act. FloodGuard AI converts raw telemetry into risk levels forecasts inundation extents affected infrastructure counts and alerts with provenance. A single physical ESP32 device posts HTTPS telemetry every few seconds. The backend validates the payload checks identity checks rate limits resolves the device stores the reading assesses risk generates forecasts for plus 15 plus 30 and plus 60 minutes runs an elevation based flood simulation publishes realtime events and evaluates alert rules. The frontend polls and subscribes and renders dashboard prediction two dimensional map three dimensional twin simulator alerts and data provenance pages.

- Summary capability 10 dash A. Secure ingestion with bearer device tokens hashed with SHA256 and constant time comparison
- Summary capability 10 dash B. Validated storage in PostGIS with UTC timestamps and indexed time series
- Summary capability 10 dash C. Explainable risk scoring with four weighted components and terrain context
- Summary capability 10 dash D. Random Forest forecasting with persistence baseline and measured skill
- Summary capability 10 dash E. Elevation threshold inundation with connectivity masking and vectorized GeoJSON
- Summary capability 10 dash F. Realtime fan out through Redis pub slash sub bridged to Socket dot IO
- Summary capability 10 dash G. Command centre console with seven routes and honest source labels

Summary synthesis 10. The result is not a sensor demo and not a dashboard mockup but a connected pipeline where a pour of water near a sensor can within seconds move a chart move a forecast move a map polygon move a three dimensional water plane and raise an alert with severity and trigger detail.

FloodGuard AI converts raw telemetry into risk levels forecasts inundation extents affected infrastructure counts and alerts with provenance. A single physical ESP32 device posts HTTPS telemetry every few seconds. The backend validates the payload checks identity checks rate limits resolves the device stores the reading assesses risk generates forecasts for plus 15 plus 30 and plus 60 minutes runs an elevation based flood simulation publishes realtime events and evaluates alert rules. The frontend polls and subscribes and renders dashboard prediction two dimensional map three dimensional twin simulator alerts and data provenance pages.

# 2. Problem Statement

Problem narrative 1. Floods can develop rapidly while existing monitoring can be delayed geographically limited and fragmented across sensors rain gauges and maps. Raw sensor data alone is not enough because centimetres without context do not convey urgency. Authorities and citizens need understandable risk information with location time confidence and recommended attention. Early warnings can reduce damage and improve response time only if they are timely trusted and actionable. The guiding question is how low cost IoT sensing real time cloud infrastructure and intelligent analytics can be combined to detect emerging flood risks and provide timely actionable information to stakeholders.

- Problem facet 1. Rapid onset means water can rise faster than patrols and phone trees can report
- Problem facet 2. Delayed monitoring leaves gaps between manual gauges and satellite passes
- Problem facet 3. Geographically limited coverage misses hyperlocal drains nullahs and low pockets
- Problem facet 4. Raw data without risk translation forces operators to guess thresholds
- Problem facet 5. Authorities need location time severity confidence and next update not just numbers
- Problem facet 6. Early warning only helps if trusted labelled and delivered to the right screen and siren
- Problem facet 7. Hackathon framing asks for low cost sensing plus cloud plus intelligence in one demoable loop

Problem deep dive 1. Flood risk in dense corridors like Mithi BKC to Kurla involves river levels rainfall runoff choked drainage tide backwater and encroached floodplains. A single gauge reading of 17 point 6 centimetres in Vadodara means little until mapped to 177 point 8 centimetres Mithi scale scored as HIGH with drivers and forecast as 187 point 0 191 point 2 205 point 8 across horizons. Without mapping scoring forecasting and impact translation the number cannot drive action. Without validation the number cannot be trusted. Without realtime delivery the number arrives late. The problem statement therefore demands calibration honesty and speed together.

# 3. Our Solution FloodGuard AI

Solution narrative 1. FloodGuard AI answers with an end to end pipeline from IoT sensor nodes through cloud API through data processing through database through AI slash ML engine to live dashboard and alert system. A field device reads water level rainfall and environment validates locally and posts telemetry over HTTPS. The Azure backend authenticates validates stores scores forecasts simulates and publishes. The frontend subscribes and polls and renders command centre views with provenance labels. The hero of the system is not any single model or map but the continuity where one input moves every output coherently.

- Solution pillar 1. IoT sensor nodes with validation and retry
- Solution pillar 2. Cloud API with auth validation and rate limiting
- Solution pillar 3. Data processing with UTC storage and indexing
- Solution pillar 4. Database with PostGIS geo and time series
- Solution pillar 5. AI slash ML engine with risk forecast and simulation
- Solution pillar 6. Live dashboard with charts maps twin and alerts
- Solution pillar 7. Alert system with dedup clear and acknowledge

Solution flow 1. The device reads sensors applies median filtering computes level as head height minus distance plus offset computes rainfall from tips times millimetres per tip over elapsed hours debounces rain validates range clamps 0 to 500 and builds JSON with node code water rainfall timestamp flow soil voltage event id location valid and source. It posts over HTTPS with bearer token and 10 second timeout handling 201 accepted 201 duplicate 400 audited 401 403 422 and 429 with Retry After. The backend resolves the device enforces identity match pins source to iot validates plausibility checks freshness stores telemetry snapshots risk updates node health maps to Mithi generates forecasts simulates layers evaluates alerts publishes events and returns id status risk and received timestamp. The frontend refreshes nodes summary alerts impacts demo mode then history forecasts layers and health on a 3 second cadence plus socket triggers.

# 4. System Architecture

Architecture narrative 1. The architecture separates concerns into IoT sensing cloud API data persistence intelligence and presentation while keeping a single realtime backbone. The IoT node speaks HTTPS to FastAPI. FastAPI speaks async SQLAlchemy to PostGIS and pub slash sub to Redis. Intelligence services for risk forecast simulation and alerts run in process and emit events. Socket dot IO bridged from Redis fans out to browsers. Next dot JS consumes REST and sockets through one pipeline and one Redux store. Terrain OSM models and config are versioned artefacts mounted into the container. Health probes CORS secrets and migrations are first class deployment concerns.

Architecture layer 1. At the edge the ESP32 owns sampling filtering and buffered HTTPS. In the cloud FastAPI owns routing auth validation and orchestration. PostGIS owns truth with 16 tables and GiST indexes. Redis owns speed with terrain cache forecast cache and realtime pub slash sub. Intelligence owns meaning with risk forecast simulation scenario and alert services. The browser owns understanding with Redux store single pipeline components and honest badges. Cross cutting concerns include UTC everywhere plus minus 24 hour window finite checks provenance labels LIVE versus SIMULATED versus FORECAST versus PREDICTED health degraded versus offline and migrations as truth never create all.

# 5. IoT Layer

IoT narrative 1. The IoT layer owned by Palak Modha covers hardware firmware networking and telemetry contract. The field reference uses ESP32 DevKit with water level sensing rain sensing environmental sensing communication over WiFi and power management. Firmware boots connects authenticates reads validates builds telemetry sends retries and repeats. The deployed contract uses POST to slash api slash iot slash devices slash register with a bootstrap token and POST to slash api slash iot slash telemetry with a device bearer token. Validation enforces ranges freshness idempotency and server side source pinning to iot for hardware trust.

1. IoT hardware element 1. ESP32 DevKit V1 as microcontroller with WiFi and NTP
2. IoT hardware element 2. Water level sensor with head height calibration and offset
3. IoT hardware element 3. Tipping bucket rain gauge with 0 point 279 millimetres per tip and debounce
4. IoT hardware element 4. Environmental sensing for soil flow battery and location
5. IoT hardware element 5. OLED 0 point 96 inch I2C for local display with SDA 21 SCL 22
6. IoT hardware element 6. Buzzer on 23 plus red LED on 25 plus green LED on 26 with resistors
7. IoT hardware element 7. Trigger echo divider rain pins 5 18 19 with pull up and filtering

IoT firmware step 1. Boot initializes pins display and network. Connect joins WiFi and syncs NTP to UTC with strftime year month day T hour minute second Z. Authenticate loads device token and registration code such as VAD ESP32 01 or NODE 001. Read samples distance rainfall soil battery flow and location. Validate checks less than 3 centimetres greater than 400 centimetres jumps greater than 100 centimetres and sets valid false when suspect. Create payload uses snprintf under 300 bytes with numbers not strings event id always and null battery allowed. Send posts to HTTPS 443 Azure or HTTP LAN with code token match. Retry on 5xx or timeout reuses same event id for idempotency. Repeat every 5 to 10 seconds respecting 12 per minute limit. Local thresholds with hysteresis drive OLED LED buzzer offline so field warning works without cloud.

# 6. Backend plus API Architecture

Backend narrative 1. The backend owned by Ahmad Abdullah with API architecture by Anish Chand Gupta provides ingestion validation business logic persistence intelligence orchestration and realtime emission. FastAPI routers separate IoT flood scenarios alerts demo and about concerns. Auth separates device identity from operator identity. Services separate telemetry ingest risk forecast simulation virtual sensing scenario alert demo websocket bridge rate limiting seeding caching and weather. PostGIS stores time series geo and simulation artefacts. Redis caches terrain forecasts and realtime channels. Alembic versions schema with GiST indexes and composite forecast index.

1. POST slash api slash iot slash devices slash register with bootstrap bearer creates physical or virtual node returns 43 char token once 401 409 422
2. GET slash api slash iot slash devices lists operator visible devices with code name type role location thresholds battery and timestamps
3. GET slash api slash iot slash devices slash code returns single device or 404
4. POST slash api slash iot slash telemetry with device bearer enforces rate limit identity match source pin ingest payload returns id status accepted duplicate risk level risk score received at with 400 401 403 422 429
5. GET slash api slash iot slash devices slash code slash latest returns latest reading with device versus received timestamps age risk node status type or 404
6. GET slash api slash iot slash devices slash code slash history with limit 1000 offset from to ascending recorded at 422 on bad range
7. GET slash api slash iot slash devices slash code slash risk history returns horizon risk score driver predicted components assessed at descending
8. GET slash api slash flood slash impact summary with scenario id aggregates latest depth layer per timestep to steps with area max affected counts depth range by risk input source note MODEL ESTIMATE
9. GET slash api slash flood slash nodes lists active physical ordered by code with ST Y ST X latest nulled if not recent current risk forecasts and simulation input live waiting labels mapping
10. GET slash api slash flood slash nodes slash code returns detail with risk by horizon current risk forecasts bounds full latest flow soil voltage source
11. GET slash api slash flood slash current summary returns active total offline stale highest risk node current rainfall timestamp
12. GET slash api slash flood slash forecasts slash code dedups newest per horizon empty if physical stale
13. GET slash api slash flood slash layers slash step with depth risk boundary scenario returns newest match with geojson max flooded input grid generated scenario impact note PREDICTED else 404
14. GET slash api slash flood slash layers lists layer metadata
15. GET slash api slash flood slash map layers with layer roads buildings waterways sensors bbox south west north east simplify 0 point 00004 buildings 0 point 00006 roads ST AsGeoJSON sensors via location waterways from file note ODbL 400 on bad bbox
16. POST slash api slash flood slash simulate with step scenario prefers forecast horizon equals step else latest baseline runs engine stores layers returns step max flooded layers impacts 400 if no data
17. GET slash api slash flood slash risk colors returns LOW MODERATE HIGH SEVERE to risk CSS classes
18. GET slash api slash alerts with scenario node severity type active hours limit returns alerts enriched node code trigger level threshold
19. GET slash api slash alerts slash active returns active alerts with counts critical high warning information and is active flag
20. POST slash api slash alerts slash id slash acknowledge with operator returns updated alert plus event
21. POST slash api slash alerts slash acknowledge all loops acknowledge with audit
22. GET slash api slash alerts slash history with node scenario hours limit returns history
23. GET slash api slash alerts slash network health returns per node online stale offline no data last reading minutes since battery plus summary
24. GET slash api slash scenarios slash presets returns normal heavy extreme plus runoff assumptions
25. POST slash api slash scenarios slash run with query name preset rainfall initial drainage duration validates preset creates running then async task returns id status message poll WS
26. GET slash api slash scenarios slash id returns inputs assumptions status forecasts layers 404 else
27. GET slash api slash scenarios slash id slash compare returns node peaks diffs corridor baseline scenario mean peak summary assumptions
28. GET slash api slash scenarios lists limit 20
29. DELETE slash api slash scenarios slash id deletes scenario orphans noted 404 else
30. GET slash api slash demo slash status returns mode speed recording active
31. POST slash api slash demo slash mode with live replay scenario validates stops replay clears scenario publishes mode changed
32. POST slash api slash demo slash reset deletes impacts layers alerts risks forecasts telemetry scenarios FK order clears Redis keeps nodes study roads buildings registry sources replay
33. POST slash api slash demo slash seed no op requiring registered ESP32
34. GET slash api slash demo slash recordings lists replay recordings
35. POST slash api slash demo slash recordings with name duration 300 snapshots recent telemetry to physical recording
36. POST slash api slash demo slash replay slash id slash start with speed 0 point 1 to 10 validates loads retags source mode replay timestamp now ingest same pipeline sleep delta over speed end to live 404 on ValueError
37. POST slash api slash demo slash replay slash stop stops replay task
38. GET slash api slash about slash data sources returns five ordered category name with provider resolution licence limitation
39. GET slash api slash about slash model info returns 15 30 60 with MAE RMSE baseline trained description plus persistence baseline
40. GET slash api slash about slash assumptions returns risk weights thresholds flood method grid buffer max depths limitations forecast horizons sampling window lags data priority source labels
41. GET slash api slash about slash study area returns Mithi BKC Kurla bounds representative grid description
42. GET slash api slash about slash honesty note returns prototype minutes not accuracy plus seven disclaimers
43. GET slash healthz liveness only no deps for platform polling
44. GET slash health and slash api slash health liveness plus deps database redis ingest http open meteo never raises degraded on failure
45. GET slash api index with service version docs endpoints iot monitoring scenarios alerts demo about

Backend file 1. backend slash app slash main dot py with FastAPI title FLOODGUARD AI version 1 dot 0 dot 0 lifespan that ensures PostGIS verifies schema seeds reference data starts bridge forecast service and alert engine and exposes healthz health api root and Socket dot IO ASGI mount. Key behaviours include validation before storage idempotency on event id audit of rejections constant time token comparison UTC normalization indexed queries and realtime emission after commit. Integration points include PostGIS for truth Redis for speed Socket dot IO for fan out and frontend polling as fallback. Hackathon relevance is direct because each file maps to a demoable behaviour from register to telemetry to forecast to layer to alert. Owner is Ahmad for services models and routers with Anish for architecture deployment and auth hardening.

# 7. AI slash ML Component

AI slash ML narrative 1. The intelligence owned by Kavya Bumiya combines explainable risk scoring with Random Forest forecasting and elevation simulation. Risk takes water level rainfall rise rate and soil moisture with weights 0 point 35 0 point 30 0 point 20 0 point 15 and bands that map scores to LOW MODERATE HIGH SEVERE. Forecasting takes an 11 feature vector over a 12 sample window with lags 1 2 3 6 to predict plus 15 plus 30 plus 60 minutes with plus minus 10 centimetre bounds and measured MAE improvement over persistence. Simulation interpolates water surface over terrain applies connectivity masking classifies depth risk vectorizes to GeoJSON and computes building and road impacts. The system is honest that risk is rule based version 1 and levels for training were simulated while rainfall was real IMD.

AI slash ML detail 1. Input features are water level rainfall rate of change historical window environmental parameters and upstream context. Processing cleans with finite checks engineers features with lags averages trends rise and spread trains Random Forest with 300 trees depth 14 leaf 5 seed 42 on chronological 70 15 15 split and scores risk with weighted bands. Output levels are LOW MODERATE HIGH SEVERE with scores 0 to 1 drivers and components. Datasets include IMD gridded rainfall 2019 2023 2024 with 0 point 25 degree cells and synthetic water levels disaggregated with gamma diurnal reservoir storage and lagged upstream totalling 315646 steps. Metrics show MAE 0 point 239 0 point 326 0 point 477 and RMSE 0 point 644 1 point 175 2 point 152 versus persistence 0 point 347 0 point 467 0 point 680 with skill about 31 30 29 percent. Bounds are hard coded plus minus 10 centimetres and disclosed as prototype. Importances show current dominates at 0 point 9972 0 point 9891 0 point 9428 with rain average only notable at 60 minutes. If rule based do not mislabel as ML and distinguish future ML with real levels uncertainty and calibration.

# 8. Frontend

Frontend narrative 1. The frontend owned by Zankhana Rajput is a Next dot JS 16 React 19 TypeScript command centre with seven routes namely Dashboard AI Prediction 2D Flood Map 3D Digital Twin What If Simulator Alerts and Monitoring and About This Data. Global state lives in Redux Toolkit with a single realtime hook mounted once in Shell. API access lives in one client with timeout and typed errors. Sockets use socket dot io client with websocket plus polling and infinite reconnect. Maps use Leaflet vector only without tiles. Twin uses Three dot JS WebGL with Gerstner water. Charts use Recharts with observed solid forecast dashed and backend bounds only. Styling uses Tailwind plus design tokens and honest empty states that show em dash WAITING and NO DATA instead of zero.

# 9. Cloud slash DevOps

Cloud narrative 1. The cloud owned by Anish Chand Gupta delivers containerization CI slash CD Azure deployment environment configuration secrets management health checks logging scaling and HTTPS. GitHub Actions builds and pushes to Azure Container Registry then updates Azure Container Apps with health polling. The Dockerfile is multi stage python 3 point 11 slim with GDAL NetCDF OpenBLAS runtime libs non root appuser healthcheck and release entrypoint that waits for DB ensures PostGIS upgrades Alembic and optionally loads OSM. Compose provides local parity with PostGIS 16 Redis 7 backend and frontend host workflow. Bicep provisions ACR Postgres Flexible Redis environment and app with secrets references and scale rules.

Cloud detail 1. GitHub hosts code with workflows deploy backend on push to main building and pushing floodguardacr floodguard backend sha then updating container app and polling 30 times 10 seconds for Running and healthz plus infra deploy manual Bicep. Docker builder installs build essential gcc g plus plus libpq dev GDAL NetCDF OpenBLAS then pip prefix install. Runtime installs libpq5 GDAL NetCDF OpenBLAS GDAL bin curl copies install copies app alembic scripts config models data creates media audio sets non root appuser exposes 8000 healthchecks curl healthz 30 10 40 3 entrypoints release then uvicorn single worker. Compose runs db postgis 16 redis 7 backend with mounts env ports depends healthy plus migrate one shot. Azure provisions ACR Basic PG16 B1ms 32GB floodguard DB Redis Basic C0 TLS Env App external 1 to 3 replicas 1CPU 2GiB http 50 concurrent sticky WS secrets for acr db redis jwt iot env for database redis jwt iot app env production socketio true frontend origin. Env requires DATABASE URL with sslmode REDIS rediss JWT hex32 IOT hex16 FRONTEND ORIGIN with optional socketio release OSM synthetic false cesium. Cost is about 7 to 13k rupees per month. Rollback activates prior revision.

# 10. Security

Security narrative 1. Security treats field devices browsers cloud secrets and database as distinct trust zones. Devices authenticate with high entropy bearer tokens stored only as SHA256 hashes compared in constant time with 401 for unknown and 403 for deactivated. Registration requires a bootstrap token never stored in plaintext and never exposed in the report. Browsers use operator identity without device tokens and all console reads use operator auth. HTTPS terminates at Azure with CORS allowlisting via FRONTEND ORIGIN. Validation rejects out of range implausible and stale timestamps and audits rejections for fault detection. Rate limiting enforces 12 per minute with 429 and Retry After. Database uses least privilege credentials and SSL require outside local hosts.

Security control 1. Device tokens are 32 bytes urlsafe shown once hashed SHA256 hex compared with hmac compare digest against dummy to avoid timing oracle with 401 for missing unknown and 403 for inactive. Registration token is exact match bootstrap only with 401 else and 409 on duplicate code and plaintext never stored. Operator identity is dashboard placeholder with acknowledged by audit and future real auth drop in. CORS uses is origin allowed with FRONTEND ORIGIN plus regex and no wildcard in production. Validation uses Pydantic for shape plus ingest for plausibility with audit table rejected readings feeding fault alerts at 3 per hour. Secrets live in Container App secrets and Compose env not in repo with rotation via az containerapp secret set update and secretref. Database appends ssl require outside local hosts and uses pool pre ping. Cloud uses non root user minimal runtime libs and health checks. Report never exposes real tokens and IOT dot md example bearer must be treated as compromised and rotated.

# 11. End to End Demonstration

Demonstration narrative 1. The end to end demonstration proves the system is one pipeline not separate components. A sensor detects rising water and the ESP32 collects and posts telemetry. The Azure backend receives validates stores and snapshots risk. The demo pipeline maps the physical level to Mithi scale. Forecast service predicts three horizons. Risk engine scores current and forecast. Simulation engine builds depth risk and boundary layers with impacts. Alert engine evaluates threshold rapid predicted communication and fault rules. Redis bridge emits to sockets. Dashboard hero KPIs chart sensor list impact alerts and drivers update. Map polygons and twin water plane move with timeline NOW plus 15 plus 30 plus 60 and play. Screenshots at each stage would show WAITING turning to LIVE with numbers and colours changing coherently.

The Azure backend receives validates stores and snapshots risk. The demo pipeline maps the physical level to Mithi scale. Forecast service predicts three horizons. Risk engine scores current and forecast. Simulation engine builds depth risk and boundary layers with impacts. Alert engine evaluates threshold rapid predicted communication and fault rules. Screenshots at each stage would show WAITING turning to LIVE with numbers and colours changing coherently.

Demo step 1. Step one IoT detects rising water with median filtering and valid flag. Step two ESP32 posts telemetry with event id and UTC Z. Step three Azure receives at slash api slash iot slash telemetry validates auth rate and schema. Step four backend stores telemetry with UTC received at and risk snapshot. Step five demo pipeline maps 0 to 30 physical to 118 to 220 Mithi with rain factor 0 point 8. Step six forecast service builds 11 features predicts 15 30 60 with bounds and input source iot demo. Step seven risk engine scores current and horizons with drivers. Step eight simulation interpolates surface masks connectivity vectorizes layers and computes impacts. Step nine alert engine creates or updates threshold rapid predicted comm fault alerts with severity and trigger data. # 12. Testing and Results

Testing narrative 1. Testing combines automated contracts unit checks live smoke and honest failure analysis. Backend pytest covers GeoJSON contract and virtual sensor lag query with 28 tests. Frontend node test covers constants and format with 23 tests. Manual smoke covers health about register spaced telemetry nodes impact layers map counts twin alerts timeline scenarios replay reset and network health. Rate limit was verified with rapid sends showing 12 accepted then throttles. Freshness gates stale after 5 minutes and offline after 15 minutes were verified. Known failures include a label rename test expecting LIVE HARDWARE versus REAL IoT INPUT and compare keys that frontend derives when null. Performance notes highlight raster interpolation and vectorization as dominant costs with GiST keeping geo queries cheap.

# 13. Innovation and Competitive Advantage

Innovation narrative 1. Judges should care because FloodGuard AI is an end to end architecture from IoT to cloud to AI to API to dashboard to alert rather than an isolated prototype. It provides continuous telemetry with validation and provenance. It converts raw values into understandable risk with drivers and plain language. It is cloud native with containers CI slash CD health probes and scaling. It is modular so additional sensors and nodes can be added without redesign. It focuses on actionable information with severity trigger detail acknowledge workflow and timeline rehearsal rather than merely displaying sensor values.

Advantage 1. End to end continuity means one pour moves charts forecasts polygons twin water and alerts together which isolated prototypes cannot show. Realtime means 3 second polling plus socket push with degraded versus offline honesty and stale versus offline per node health. Intelligence means explainable risk with components drivers and plain language plus measured Random Forest skill versus persistence with caveats. Cloud native means Docker CI slash CD Azure health scaling and secrets discipline. Modularity means new sensors via register plus relationships plus virtual propagation without redesign. Actionability means severity trigger detail acknowledge workflow scenario rehearsal and impact counts for buildings roads area max depth and depth range rather than raw numbers alone.

# 15. Future Scope

Future narrative 1. Future scope stays specific to flood resilience rather than generic. Near term adds LoRaWAN long range networks solar power more distributed nodes ML prediction with real levels satellite and weather fusion GIS risk maps SMS WhatsApp notifications mobile app sirens edge processing and authority integration. Medium term adds calibration with surveyed cross sections tide and drainage coupling uncertainty bands from tree quantiles and data retention policies. Long term adds city scale mesh rescue allocation and digital twin fidelity with surveyed buildings and high resolution DEM. Each future item maps to a current seam such as transport firmware power model training or simulation resolution.

1. Future item. LoRaWAN long range mesh to extend beyond WiFi with gateway backhaul and delay tolerant buffering
2. Future item. Solar powered nodes with battery sizing sleep scheduling and brownout safe firmware
3. Future item. Denser corridor mesh with upstream midstream downstream roles and calibrated delays attenuations
4. Future item. ML prediction with real Mithi levels uncertainty bands tree quantiles and online recalibration
5. Future item. Satellite and weather fusion with GPM IMERG Open Meteo IMD downscaling and tide coupling
6. Future item. GIS risk maps with parcel road building exposure and evacuation routing
7. Future item. SMS WhatsApp siren mobile app notifications with severity templates and quiet hours
8. Future item. Edge processing with local risk scoring store and forward and offline display
9. Future item. Authority integration with SOP playbooks audit trails and role based access
10. Future item. High resolution DEM surveyed cross sections drainage capacity and hydraulic calibration
11. Future item. Data retention compaction and lifecycle for forecasts layers telemetry and impacts
12. Future item. Chaos testing fault injection and red team validation for comm loss sensor drift and replay attacks

Chaos maps to rejected readings fault alerts and network health.

Assurance expansion 1. FloodGuard AI keeps every value traceable to source timestamp and assumption. Live hardware is labelled REAL IoT INPUT with cyan badge. Simulated propagation is labelled SIMULATED with purple badge. Forecasts are labelled FORECAST with blue badge and layers note PREDICTED MODEL ESTIMATE not official flood zone. Missing data shows em dash WAITING or NO DATA never zero. Socket down with REST ok shows DEGRADED polling REST while healthz unreachable shows OFFLINE. Physical nodes require recent IoT within 5 minutes else latest is nulled and twin shows waiting. Forecasts require 8 readings over 12 window else insufficient path. Simulation requires terrain raster or fails loudly unless synthetic opt in which is labelled SIMULATED never cached as real. Alerts dedup by node type scenario horizon trigger keep severe recent supersede rest audit superseded by and clear with events. Scenarios run async with poll and WS and compare with peak mean diffs and summary sentence. Reset deletes seven tables in FK order and clears Redis while keeping nodes study OSM registry sources replay. This discipline is what makes the demo trustworthy for judges operators and planners.
